KNOWN BUG: The combobox tracks the active option by index, so after the options change while it is open, Enter commits a different option than the highlighted one.

Rules:

- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Nested Dialog, Escape: inner `Escape` also calls the outer `onOpenChange(false)`. Repro: outer open, inner opened from an outer button, `{Escape}` → outer mock called 1 time (expected 0). Cause: React events bubble through the portal to the outer `onKeyDown`.
- [blocking] Nested Dialog, Tab trap: `Tab` from the inner dialog's middle button moves focus to the outer dialog's first tabbable (`openinner` button behind the inner modal). Expected `i2`. The outer handler computes tabbables from its own DOM, which excludes the portal.
- [blocking] Dialog focus lost: removing the focused button inside the dialog leaves `document.activeElement` as BODY. Escape then does not call `onOpenChange` (calls = 0), and Tab bypasses the trap. Same result after a programmatic blur to body.
- [blocking] Dialog backdrop: mousedown on backdrop, mouseup inside content, click (common ancestor = backdrop) → `onOpenChange(false)` fires. The code checks only the press, while its comment says press and release. This contradicts "clicks inside the content do not close it".
- [blocking] Tabs T5: a tab with `aria-disabled="true"` (passed via rest, not `disabled`) can be selected by click. `onValueChange("b")` fires, and the uncontrolled internal state becomes "b" while `aria-selected` stays false. Later enabling that tab would jump selection. `select()` and `Tab`'s onClick never check `isEnabledTab`.
- [blocking] Tabs: the selected tab is disabled, or removed, by a memoized child's own state (TabList's layout effect does not re-run). Result: no enabled tab has tabIndex 0, so the tablist is unreachable by Tab. Repro: "expected +0 to be 1".
- [minor] Clicking the Combobox input does not open the list (`aria-expanded` stays false). Criteria only require typing or ArrowDown, so this is a UX note; not a criteria failure.
- [minor] `getByLabelText("Fruit")` matches both the input and the listbox (listbox has `aria-labelledby`). Not reproduced as a functional problem.
- [minor] Dialog `className`/`rest` lands on the inner `role="dialog"` element, not the backdrop. G2 "root" is ambiguous; README says "root element".
- [minor] README says "when the query is empty, no option is active", but ArrowDown with empty text activates the first option. Not reproduced as a bug in the typing path.
- [minor] Controlled Tabs ignoring the callback: ArrowRight moves DOM focus to B while A stays selected (tabIndex 0 remains on A). Matches README; noted only.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog stack order is wrong when nested dialogs mount open together. Child layout effects run before the parent's, so the outer is pushed last and becomes "top". Probe: `<Dialog open onOpenChange={outer}><button>ob</button><Dialog open onOpenChange={inner}><button>i1</button></Dialog></Dialog>`. Result: focus at mount is `ob` (not `i1`), Escape gives `OUTER CALLS: 1 INNER CALLS: 0`. This breaks README line 91 ("an inner dialog never closes or hands focus to the outer one") and criterion D5/nesting. Fix idea: push the token in a way that orders by DOM/tree depth, or defer the outer push, not by effect order.
- [minor] The same mount-order issue likely affects focus restore on nested close, but I did not reproduce that.
- [minor] README line 109 says Escape "stops propagation" only for Combobox; the Dialog relies on `defaultPrevented`, so any third-party Escape handler that calls `preventDefault` will silently block dialog close. Design note, not reproduced as a defect.

=== IMPLEMENTOR HANDOFF 2 (sent after review 2) ===
GOAL: Fix one reproduced bug in src/Dialog/Dialog.tsx of /tmp/ff-eval-nxf4w7gq/workspace (uncommitted work; read the file first) and add regression tests in src/Dialog/Dialog.test.tsx.

Bug: the module-level `openDialogs` stack is ordered by layout-effect order. When nested dialogs mount open in the same commit, the child's effect runs before the parent's, so the outer dialog is pushed last and treated as top-most. Repro: `<Dialog open title="Outer" onOpenChange={outer}><button>ob</button><Dialog open title="Inner" onOpenChange={inner}><button>i1</button></Dialog></Dialog>`. Focus at mount lands on `ob` instead of `i1`, and Escape calls outer once and inner zero times. Expected: focus on `i1`, and Escape calls only `inner`.

Required fix: add a small internal React context (not exported) that gives each Dialog's subtree its nesting depth (parent depth + 1, top level 0). Store `{ depth }` tokens in the stack and keep it ordered by depth, with insertion order breaking ties (a later sibling at the same depth is top). Insert at the right position instead of push+sort if that's simpler. Only move focus into the dialog on open when it is top-most after insertion, so an outer dialog mounting in the same commit as its open child doesn't steal focus. Everything else stays: document keydown/focusin listeners gated on top-most, Escape skipping defaultPrevented, focus restore to the previous element on close/unmount, the backdrop press+release logic.

Tests to add: (a) the repro above, asserting focus on i1, Escape calls only inner, and Tab stays in inner; (b) after the inner closes (parent sets its open=false), the outer becomes top: Escape calls outer and Tab is trapped in the outer; (c) existing nested-later-open tests still pass.
